content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves an Isaiah 7:14 link by reference to cited verses and says the point was answered in [CR2] and [CR3], so it engages K-G4's rule about counting verses as unanswered witnesses.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.","room":"counts as an unanswered witness: (1) treating any verse mentioned in the balance as counting versus (2) only treating a verse as unanswered and counted toward a broken link; the judge text labels the point answered and gives no pressed-sentence quote, so it does not count an unanswered witness.","why":"The judge says the Isaiah 7:14 point was answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5 and does not count any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link, so the K-G4 quotation-and-naming requirement is not triggered."}
